tools.name: share_markdown
tools.description: Publish markdown at a public docs-md.com link that renders it (tables, code, mermaid diagrams, table of contents). Use it to send a plan, spec, report, README or agent handoff to a person or another agent. Returns the URL, a raw-markdown URL and an edit token for later updates or deletion.

tools.name: update_share
tools.description: Replace the content of an existing share using its id and edit token.

tools.name: read_share
tools.description: Fetch the raw markdown of a docs-md.com share. Accepts the share id or any docs-md.com share URL. Use it when someone gives you a docs-md.com link, for example a handoff written by another agent.

tools.name: delete_share
tools.description: Permanently delete a share using its id and edit token.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: read_share · Private data: share_markdown, update_share, delete_share · Public sink: share_markdown, update_share, read_share, delete_share · Destructive: delete_share.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: read_share · Private data: share_markdown, update_share, delete_share · Public sink: share_markdown, update_share, read_share, delete_share · Destructive: delete_share

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
